author_or_org: Fasheng Xu, Jing Hou, Wei Chen, Karen Xie

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: GenAI's intrinsic fallibility, producing confident but incorrect outputs, requires continuous human oversight.
claims.quote: Unlike earlier automation technologies, GenAI can both perform tasks autonomously and assist human workers, while its intrinsic fallibility, the tendency to produce confident but incorrect outputs, demands continuous human oversight.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The effect of GenAI on entry-level skill requirements depends critically on whether it is deployed as automation or augmentation.
claims.quote: First, GenAI's effect on entry-level skill requirements is critically mode-dependent.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Worker-level automation leads firms to hire fewer but more skilled workers who validate AI outputs and limit costly escalation to experts.
claims.quote: Worker-level automation leads firms to hire fewer but more skilled workers who validate AI outputs and limit costly escalation to experts.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Worker-level augmentation expands workers' effective capability, allowing firms to relax entry-level knowledge requirements while sustaining performance.
claims.quote: Worker-level augmentation, by contrast, expands workers' effective capability, allowing firms to relax entry-level knowledge requirements while sustaining performance.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The documented decline in junior employment reflects deployment choices favoring automation over augmentation, not an inevitable consequence of GenAI itself.
claims.quote: The decline in junior employment documented in recent studies therefore reflects deployment choices favoring automation over augmentation, not an inevitable consequence of GenAI itself.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Expert-level deployment uniformly lowers entry-level skill requirements, regardless of whether GenAI automates or augments.
claims.quote: Second, expert-level deployment uniformly lowers entry-level skill requirements, regardless of whether GenAI automates or augments.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: By expanding experts' capacity to support downstream workers, expert-level deployment enables organizations to employ a broader base of less specialized workers, broadening entry-level access to knowledge work.
claims.quote: By expanding experts' capacity to support downstream workers, it enables organizations to employ a broader base of less specialized workers, thereby broadening entry-level access to knowledge work.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Organizational structure evolves non-monotonically as GenAI improves: the span of control initially contracts before eventually expanding across all four deployment architectures.
claims.quote: Third, organizational structure evolves non-monotonically as GenAI improves: across all four deployment architectures, the span of control initially contracts before eventually expanding.
